title: Argo float programme
summary: Argo is an international programme of autonomous profiling floats that measure temperature and salinity in the upper 2,000 meters of the global ocean. NOAA says it began in 1998 when the Argo Science Team proposed a global array, with float deployments starting in 1999, and that the 3,000-float goal was reached in November 2007. It now involves 34 countries and has deployed more than 15,000 floats.

uncertainty.note: The id says 2000; the pages give 1998 (proposal), 1999 (first deployments) and Oct or Nov 2007 (3,000 floats). The programme continues. End year marks the 3,000-float milestone.
